title.value: Tracking and predicting COVID‐19 radiological trajectory on chest X‐rays using deep learning
title.justification: The title directly reflects the core focus of the paper, which is on tracking and predicting the radiological trajectory of COVID-19 using deep learning technologies.
title.quote:
Tracking and predicting COVID‐19 radiological trajectory on chest
X‐rays using deep learning

extractions.description: This paper discusses the application of deep learning technologies to track and predict the future radiological trajectory of COVID‐19 patients using chest X‐ray images. It utilizes deep learning algorithms repurposed for feature extraction and classical machine-learning algorithms for evaluating disease severity and potential trajectory from X-ray data.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper's primary focus is on healthcare improvements related to COVID-19 diagnosis and prediction using deep learning, not directly on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Radiological findings on chest X-ray (CXR) have shown to be essential for the proper management of COVID-19 patients... We trained a repurposed deep learning algorithm on the CheXnet open dataset...

primary_category.justification: The central theme of the paper is related to healthcare and AI in medical imaging, rather than Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: We hypothesize that deep learning can be harnessed to analyze CXRs and extract radiological features in a reproducible and quantitative manner.

secondary_categories.justification: There were no secondary themes related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development in the paper.
secondary_categories.quote: Clinical prediction rules are therefore required to help caregivers during this delicate but necessary decision making process, and these rules should be based in part on the prognosis of possible ­outcomes.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no sub-category applicable under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as the focus is purely on medical imaging for COVID-19.
primary_sub_category.quote: Deep learning predictions between “Worse” and “Improved” outcome categories and for severity stratification were significantly different for three radiological signs and one diagnostic...

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Sub-categories related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development are not addressed in the paper.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The main finding over time on CXR was consolidation. These findings are not specific however, as they are similar to other causes of coronavirus and other viral pneumonias.

applications.justification: The paper focuses on predicting the radiological trajectory of COVID-19 using machine learning and deep learning models on X-ray image data.
applications.quote: CXR deep learning features show promise for classifying disease severity and trajectory.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not fit any existing Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories as it is focused on medical imaging for COVID-19.
new_primary_category.quote: Triage decisions to decide if and when patients should be admitted to the ICU and be mechanically ventilated during the current COVID-19 pandemic must be based on all available prognostic evidence.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is needed as the paper's focus lies outside Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: ...use a deep learning architecture, pre-trained on a large CXR dataset, and able to learn image features related to nine radiological signs and one pneumonia diagnosis.
